pr.title: fix: History changes indicator missing on load and stuck on "N changes"
pr.author: Tom Moor
commitTitles: fix: History changes indicator missing on load and stuck on "N changes"
fix: Match changes param check to RevisionViewer
fix: Disable change nav buttons until Diff extension is available
fix: Reset changes count only on unmount to avoid flicker

summary.problem: In document history, the header's changes counter didn't appear on load and got stuck, because it read the count through a non-reactive editor ref that is set late and replaced on remount.
summary.solution: Compute the count from the changeset where it is already built, publish it through the observable DocumentContext, and make the editor reference observable too.

steps.title: The changes counter is missing or stuck
steps.narration: When you look at an older version of a document, the header shows how many changes it contains and lets you jump between them. According to the pull request, that counter often doesn't appear at all, and when it does, it gets stuck instead of showing which change you're on. The counter is drawn in the header, so that's where we start.

beats.heading: How it works now
beats.text: `ChangesNavigation` renders the counter in the revision header. It decides whether to render from the URL, then reads the count from the editor's Diff extension.

lines.annotation: Turns the whole counter on or off based on the URL.
The count lives inside the editor: ref → editor → extensions → Diff.
With a count of 0 the counter renders nothing.

sources.ref: fix: History changes indicator missing on load and stuck on "N changes"

steps.headline: The change counter is missing or stuck
steps.say: When you open an older version, the header should say how many changes there are and let you step through them.

items: The counter doesn’t appear when the page loads
When it does, it stays on “N changes” instead of “2 of N”

steps.title: Small cause: get() versus has()
steps.narration: First, a small mismatch. Two parts of the page check the same flag in the address bar, but in different ways. If the flag is present without a value, one part says yes and the other says no, so the changes are highlighted in the text while the counter stays hidden.

beats.heading: How it works now
beats.text: The same `changes` URL parameter is read in two places, with two different methods.

lines.annotation: Asks: does the parameter have a non-empty value?
Asks: is the parameter present at all? Decides whether highlights are built.

beats.heading: What breaks
beats.text: With a link like `?changes` (no value) the two checks disagree.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: Both places now ask the same question, so highlights and counter switch on together.

notes: That links of the form ?changes (without a value) exist in the app is inferred from the commit title; the analyzer did not locate where they are generated.

sources.ref: Match changes param check to RevisionViewer

steps.headline: Two parts read the same link differently
steps.say: For a link ending in “?changes”, the text shows highlights, but the counter decides changes are off.
steps.check: Both now ask “is the flag there?”. Should a flag with no value turn changes on?

steps.title: How the header gets the editor
steps.narration: The header reaches the editor through a reference that is handed down from the page, through the header, into the counter. The catch is that updating such a reference never tells anyone to redraw. So the header only notices the editor when it happens to redraw for some unrelated reason.

beats.heading: How it works now
beats.text: `editorRef` is prop-drilled from `Document` through `Header` into `ChangesNavigation`. Setting `ref.current` does not re-render, and MobX `observer` cannot track it.

lines.annotation: The counter reads the editor from a ref, which is not reactive.

steps.headline: The header hears about the editor by chance
steps.say: The editor is passed down through a handle that never announces changes. The header only notices it when it redraws for some other reason.

visual.caption: The editor travels down through two components, and nobody is told when it changes.

steps.title: The editor appears late, and more than once
steps.narration: The editor that draws the highlighted text is loaded lazily, and it is rebuilt from scratch when the older version it compares against finishes loading. So on the first draw the header sees no editor at all, and after the rebuild it keeps looking at the old one.

beats.heading: How it works now
beats.text: This was already documented in a code comment: the editor is remounted via `key` whenever the diff configuration or the comparison data changes.

lines.text: // The editor builds its extensions once, on mount, so it has to be remounted
// whenever the diff configuration changes. Revisions are listed without their
// content, so the revision being compared against — and with it the Diff
// extension — usually only arrives on a later render; without this neither
// the highlights nor the change count would ever appear.

lines.annotation: The key flips when comparison data arrives → new editor instance.
The editor is also published to DocumentContext, but that field is not observable yet.

notes: The mechanism behind "stuck" (header still observing the previous Diff instance while buttons drive the new one) is the analyzer's inference from code, not described by the author.
steps.headline: The editor arrives late, then gets rebuilt
steps.say: On the first draw there is no editor yet. Later it is rebuilt from scratch, and the header keeps looking at the old one.

steps.title: Make the editor reactive
steps.narration: The editor was already being stored in a shared place for the document, but nobody could subscribe to it. Now that slot notifies anyone who reads it, so the header redraws the moment the editor appears or is replaced.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: `editor` in `DocumentContext` becomes a MobX observable reference.

lines.text: /** The editor instance for this document */

lines.annotation: `.ref` tracks only replacement of the reference; MobX won't try to make the whole ProseMirror editor deeply observable.

steps.headline: The shared editor slot now announces changes
steps.say: The editor was already kept in a shared place for the document. Now anything that reads it redraws when the editor appears or is replaced.
steps.check: Everything reading this slot now redraws when the editor changes. Anything expensive among them?

steps.title: The counter doesn't need the editor at all
steps.narration: Making the editor reactive fixes the stuck counter, but the number would still only show up after the editor loads. The key idea of this change: the number of changes depends only on the difference between two versions, not on the editor. So the counting logic is pulled out into a function that works without an editor.

beats.heading: How it works now
beats.text: Counting is an instance method, so it needs a mounted `Diff` extension.

lines.annotation: Needs an instance: only reachable through a mounted editor.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: The same logic moves to a static method; the instance method now delegates to it. Behaviour of counting is unchanged.

sources.ref: app/scenes/Document/components/RevisionViewer.tsx: "so the indicator can render before the editor ... finished mounting"

steps.headline: Decision: counting doesn’t need the editor
steps.say: The number depends only on the two versions being compared. So the counting moves into a function that works without any editor.
steps.check: The counting is moved, not rewritten. Does the diff confirm the logic is identical?

steps.title: Count where the changeset already exists
steps.narration: The difference between the two versions is already calculated in the component that shows the old version. Now the count is taken from that same calculation and put into the shared document state, so the header gets it immediately instead of waiting for the editor.

beats.heading: How it works now
beats.text: The changeset is computed here and its only consumer is the `Diff` extension passed into the editor.

lines.annotation: The difference between the two revisions.
The only consumer of the changeset.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: The memo now returns both the extensions and the count, and the count is published to the context.

lines.annotation: Count and highlights come from the same changeset in the same memo, so they cannot diverge.

steps.headline: Count right where the difference is made
steps.say: The viewer already works out the difference to highlight it. Now it also takes the count from there and puts it in the shared state.
steps.check: When highlights are off the count is 0. Is that the right value to publish?

steps.title: A channel between the viewer and the header
steps.narration: Back to the shared document state. The component that knows the count and the header that shows it aren't directly connected, so a shared observable value is the shortest path between them. The same place already carries the editor, so an existing channel is extended rather than a new one invented.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: A new observable `totalChanges` with an action setter.

lines.text: /** The total number of changes in the currently viewed revision diff */

notes: Not chosen (inferred): passing the count down through Document and Header as props — that prop chain was the source of the problem.
steps.headline: The viewer and the header share one number
steps.say: They aren’t connected directly, so the number travels through the shared document state, the same place that already holds the editor.

visual.caption: The count now goes from the viewer into shared state, and the header reads it from there.

steps.check: The new totalChanges field is read from the same context as editor. Does anything else read totalChanges before this step publishes it?

steps.title: Reset only on unmount
steps.narration: There was one more iteration. If the count is cleared every time it's recalculated, it drops to zero for a moment whenever you switch versions, and the header blinks. So clearing was moved to a separate step that only runs when you leave the history view.

beats.heading: What broke in the first version
beats.text: Likely intermediate version: reset in the cleanup of the publishing effect.

beats.text: A separate effect with stable deps runs its cleanup only on unmount.

lines.text: // Reset the count on unmount so it does not linger on the live document.

lines.annotation: Two effects instead of one: publishing and resetting have different lifetimes.

steps.title: The header reads from the context
steps.narration: Now the number arrives immediately, while the editor may still be loading. That's why the last commit disables the previous and next buttons until the editor is ready; otherwise they would appear together with the number but do nothing.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: No more props: the counter takes `editor` and `totalChanges` from context; navigation buttons are disabled until the Diff extension exists.

plain.title: The history counter shows up at once and keeps counting
plain.problem: In document history, the change counter often doesn’t appear, and when it does it gets stuck on “N changes”.
plain.fix: Count the changes where the comparison is already made, and hand the number to the header directly.
